concepts.name: Definition and Core Mechanics of Climate Tipping Points
key_dimensions: Distinction between 'tipping point' vs 'tipping element' vs 'threshold' — UPSC often conflates these
Non-linearity and irreversibility: why small forcing causes disproportionate system response
Difference between fast tipping points (years) and slow tipping points (centuries) and their policy implications
IPCC AR6 definition vs Lenton et al. (2008) foundational framework — which is authoritative

concepts.name: West Antarctic Ice Sheet (WAIS) Collapse as a Tipping Element
key_dimensions: Marine Ice Sheet Instability (MISI) mechanism and the role of bedrock topography
Threshold temperature range: estimated at 1.5–2°C global warming — overlap with Paris Agreement targets
Projected sea level rise contribution: up to 3–5 metres over centuries — distinction from Greenland contribution
Recent findings on Thwaites Glacier as the 'weak underbelly' and its cascading potential

concepts.name: Greenland Ice Sheet Tipping Point
key_dimensions: Surface Mass Balance feedback vs dynamic ice flow feedback — mechanistic difference
Estimated tipping threshold: ~1.5–2°C, but full melt takes millennia — trap: timescale confusion
Sea level contribution: ~7 metres if fully melted — contrast with WAIS figures
Meltwater pulse impact on AMOC — illustrates cascade/domino tipping point concept

concepts.name: Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) Collapse
key_dimensions: Mechanism: freshwater influx from ice melt disrupting thermohaline density gradient
Consequences: European cooling paradox amid global warming — frequently tested contrast
AMOC weakening vs full collapse — current evidence (Caesar et al., 2021) and debate on imminence
Interaction with monsoon systems including Indian Summer Monsoon — direct UPSC relevance

concepts.name: Amazon Rainforest Dieback as a Tipping Element
key_dimensions: Dual drivers: climate change-induced drought AND deforestation — synergistic effect
Savannification threshold: estimated at ~20–25% deforestation (currently ~17%) — specific figures matter
Flying rivers concept: Amazon's role in moisture recycling for South American and potentially South Asian precipitation
Carbon store to carbon source transition — net radiative forcing implications for global targets

concepts.name: Permafrost Thaw and Carbon Feedback Loop
key_dimensions: Distinction between gradual permafrost thaw vs abrupt thermokarst formation — two different processes
Carbon stock locked in permafrost: ~1,500 Gt C — comparison with current atmospheric carbon (~880 Gt C)
CH4 vs CO2 release ratio and why methane dominates short-term warming potential from permafrost
Permafrost thaw as a 'sleeping giant' feedback — why it is excluded from most IPCC baseline models (trap)

concepts.name: Coral Reef Systems as Ecological Tipping Elements
key_dimensions: Dual stressors: ocean warming (bleaching) AND ocean acidification — mechanistic distinction
Thermal threshold: sustained temperatures 1°C above mean summer maximum triggers mass bleaching
Regime shift from coral-dominated to algae-dominated systems — ecological tipping point concept
Great Barrier Reef, Lakshadweep, and Gulf of Mannar — India-specific coral tipping point relevance

concepts.name: Boreal Forest (Taiga) Dieback
key_dimensions: Mechanism: warming-induced pest outbreaks, fire frequency increase, and drought stress
Albedo feedback: boreal forest replacement by shrubs/grassland reduces surface albedo and amplifies warming
Carbon stock significance: boreal forests store ~30% of terrestrial carbon
Interaction with permafrost tipping point — overlapping geographic zone creates compound risk

concepts.name: Arctic Sea Ice Loss (Summer Ice-Free Arctic) Tipping Point
key_dimensions: Ice-Albedo feedback mechanism: self-reinforcing loop once ice area falls below critical threshold
Projections: first ice-free Arctic summer possible before 2050 at current trajectories
Arctic amplification: Arctic warming 2–4x faster than global average — mechanism and consequences
Jet stream disruption and extreme weather teleconnections including Indian heatwaves and floods

concepts.name: Monsoon System Tipping Points (Indian Summer Monsoon and West African Monsoon)
key_dimensions: Indian Summer Monsoon weakening vs intensification debate — aerosol forcing vs GHG forcing conflict
Land-sea thermal gradient as the fundamental driver and how tipping disrupts it
West African monsoon as a tipping element with historical evidence (Green Sahara to Sahara transition ~5,500 BP)
AMOC collapse → ISM weakening cascade — multi-system interaction for Mains answers

concepts.name: Cascade Effects and Tipping Point Interactions ('Domino Effect')
key_dimensions: Lenton et al. (2018) 'Hothouse Earth' pathway — specific concept name and threshold (~2°C)
Network analysis of tipping elements: which ones are 'hubs' with most cascade connections
Self-amplifying feedback cascade vs linear climate response — why 2°C is not 'twice as bad' as 1°C
Policy implication: why cascades justify precautionary action below modeled individual tipping thresholds

concepts.name: Temperature Thresholds and Paris Agreement Overlap
key_dimensions: Why 1.5°C is a critical threshold: number of tipping elements activated at 1.5°C vs 2°C vs 3°C
Committed warming vs equilibrium warming — tipping points can be crossed even with current concentrations
Carbon budget remaining for 1.5°C: ~500 GtCO2 (IPCC AR6) — and its adequacy given tipping risks
Trap: Paris Agreement 'well below 2°C' language vs scientific community's tipping point threshold concerns

concepts.name: Tipping Points vs Feedback Loops: Conceptual Distinction
key_dimensions: Positive feedback loop (amplifying) vs tipping point — a tipping point is an outcome enabled by feedbacks
Examples: Water vapor feedback, ice-albedo feedback (feedbacks) vs AMOC collapse (tipping point)
Slow feedbacks (carbon cycle, ice sheets) vs fast feedbacks (water vapor, clouds) — timescale matters
UPSC trap: questions may use 'tipping point' loosely to mean 'feedback' — precision in answers is rewarded

concepts.name: Early Warning Signals of Approaching Tipping Points
key_dimensions: Critical slowing down (CSD) as a universal early warning signal — statistical basis
Observable proxies: autocorrelation increase, variance increase in system variables before tipping
AMOC fingerprinting using sea surface temperature patterns — real-world detection application
Limitations: not all tipping elements show reliable early warnings (e.g., ENSO-related thresholds)

concepts.name: Tipping Points and Sea Level Rise: Compound Projections
key_dimensions: Distinction: thermal expansion (non-tipping, gradual) vs ice sheet collapse contribution (tipping-driven)
IPCC AR6 low-likelihood high-impact scenario: up to 2 metres by 2100 if tipping points activated
Coastal vulnerability: SIDS, Bangladesh, and Indian coastal cities (Mumbai, Chennai) — UPSC geography link
Tipping-point-driven SLR vs managed retreat policy — governance dimension for GS-2 integration

concepts.name: Societal and Economic Tipping Points Linked to Climate Tipping Elements
key_dimensions: Food system tipping: simultaneous crop failure in multiple breadbaskets triggered by climate tipping cascades
Migration tipping point: threshold number of climate refugees that overwhelms governance systems
Financial tipping point: stranded assets and insurance market collapse in fossil fuel sector
Distinction: natural system tipping points (physical) vs social system tipping points (adaptive capacity) — GS-1/GS-3 link

concepts.name: Geoengineering Responses to Tipping Points: Solar Radiation Management (SRM) and CDR
key_dimensions: SRM (Stratospheric Aerosol Injection) as emergency brake — can reduce temperature but cannot address tipping elements already crossed
Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR): DACCS, BECCS — role in buying time before tipping thresholds are crossed
Termination shock: abrupt stopping of SRM could accelerate warming and trigger multiple tipping points simultaneously
Governance vacuum: no international treaty governs geoengineering — UPSC governance angle

concepts.name: IPCC Assessment Reports and Evolving Treatment of Tipping Points
key_dimensions: AR5 vs AR6 shift: AR6 for the first time assessed tipping points with 'high confidence' for some elements
AR6 Chapter 4 (Cross-Chapter Box TIPPING): specific tipping elements assessed — which ones have highest confidence
Distinction between regional tipping points (coral reefs, monsoons) vs global tipping points (ice sheets, AMOC)
Criticism of IPCC conservatism: scientists argue IPCC underestimates tipping point risks due to consensus process

concepts.name: India-Specific Vulnerabilities to Global Tipping Points
key_dimensions: AMOC weakening → ISM disruption → agricultural and water security crisis for 1.3 billion people
Himalayan glacier retreat (Third Pole tipping) → river flow variability in Ganga-Brahmaputra-Indus systems
Coral reef tipping in Lakshadweep and Andaman — fisheries, coastal protection, and tourism economy
Permafrost thaw → methane surge → accelerated warming → compound heat stress in Indo-Gangetic Plain

concepts.name: Third Pole (Hindu Kush Himalaya) as a Regional Tipping Element
key_dimensions: Largest non-polar ice store: ~46,000 glaciers, water tower for 2 billion people across 10 river systems
Black carbon deposition accelerating melt — South Asian pollution as a regional tipping driver
Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) as near-term abrupt impact before long-term water scarcity
HKH tipping point interaction with South Asian monsoon — ICIMOD reports as authoritative source for UPSC
